title: PUCK_TIER dict lookup lost the .get(ports, 1.0) default — a SPEC-table tier edit with a missing key crashes with an unhandled KeyError
evidence:
r = PUCK_R * PUCK_TIER[ports]
PUCK_TIER      = {4: 1.0, 8: 1.15, 16: 1.30}   # tier size ladder (keep)
(removed in diff: -    scale = {4: 1.0, 8: 1.15, 16: 1.30}.get(ports, 1.0))
detail: Old code defaulted unknown port counts; the rework keys PUCK_TIER directly. The SPEC table is the declared fill-in-the-blanks edit surface — dropping/renaming a tier key while main() still passes 4/8/16 raises an unguarded KeyError mid-render.
recommended_fix: Use PUCK_TIER.get(ports) with an explicit raise listing valid keys, or assert set(PUCK_TIER) == {4, 8, 16} near the SPEC table.

title: ast.literal_eval on SPRITE_ORDER raises uncaught ValueError if the pin is ever a non-literal, bypassing the designed clean FAIL
detail: script_order handles a missing SPRITE_ORDER with a clean SystemExit FAIL, but a non-literal assignment (concatenation, call) makes literal_eval raise ValueError — a raw traceback instead of the gate's designed failure message (exit code still fails the lint gate).
recommended_fix: Wrap ast.literal_eval in try/except (ValueError, SyntaxError) and raise SystemExit with the same FAIL-style message.
